My Claude Code setup: one CLAUDE.md, a skill for every chore and parallel agents

The problem it solves

Coding agents are fast but forgetful. Every session starts from zero: they ask the same questions, pick a different style each time, make git choices I did not want and sometimes touch files I never mentioned. And once I run several agents at once, they step on each other.

The general idea

Treat the agent like a new colleague that I onboard once, in writing. A global instructions file says how I work, skills package the jobs I repeat, a permission allowlist removes the routine prompts, and every task gets its own copy of the repository. All of it lives in my dotfiles repository, so every machine behaves the same.

Examples

The heart is a global CLAUDE.md. A few lines from mine:

Version control: Git, kept minimal. When the task is finished, run the
checks, then commit only the files you changed. Nothing else: no branches,
stash, reset, clean, rebase, amend or push, and never stage unrelated files.

I am using uv. Use strict type notations and validate with pyright.
Write the tests via pytest in the tests/ folder.

And an allowlist in settings.json, so the routine steps never interrupt me:

"allow": [
  "Bash(uv run *)", "Bash(ruff *)", "Bash(pyright *)",
  "Bash(git add *)", "Bash(git commit *)"
]

Tips from my setup

  • Rules about the answers too. Blocking questions come in bold and finished items in italic, so I can skim a long reply in a second.
  • A skill for every chore. I keep around thirty-five: reading data files with DuckDB, DVC, Quarto slides, OpenAlex literature search, and git helpers such as worktree, merge, rebase and open-pr. A repeated instruction becomes a skill the second time I type it.
  • A cheap worker for cheap jobs. A small custom agent runs on Haiku and does the exploring and the paperwork for OpenSpec, so the expensive model only does the thinking. See the post about OpenSpec.
  • Parallel agents in worktrees. workmux opens a git worktree and a tmux window per task with an agent inside. Finished branches are merged by rebase, and a coordinator skill can spawn and watch several agents.
  • Strict mode when I want it. Launcher recipes start an agent that must show every diff and wait for my approval, for the code I want to read line by line.
  • Hooks tell herdr what the agent is doing, so the sidebar shows which one is working and which one is waiting for me. See the post about herdr.
